title: Choose Hermaeus’s visual world
question: The roll assigned The Black Books. Keep it, take my pick or the category standard, or re-roll.

options.label: The Black Books
options.lineage: Hermaeus Mora’s Black Books and the library-realm of Apocrypha
options.thesis: Each playthrough is a Black Book: Hermaeus is where you read and amend what SkyrimNet wrote in it.
options.viewport: A murk-green rail holds the playthrough, the quick toggles and the sections; beside it the character list and Serana’s memories as a dense glossed page, with Hermaeus’s eye in the top bar.
options.risk: The literal reading of the name: any ornament beyond type, palette and the eye turns it into a game-skin costume, and dark green must be checked hard for contrast.

raised.raise: Sigil green is reserved for things you can act on; nothing else on screen uses it.
The rail is one committed field of Apocrypha green, never a grey sidebar.
Saves stamp what they did (saved, copy updated, search vector pending) on the record itself; nothing just disappears.
Quantities are tabular figures, and importance reads as an ink density, not a number alone.
Every memory and entry carries its catalog number, quietly, so cross-references like “copy of diary entry 143” resolve at a glance.
While one record is being edited, the rest of the page dims behind it.

options.label: The Game’s Own Menus
options.lineage: Skyrim’s journal, map and SkyUI inventory menus
options.thesis: Hermaeus as one more menu of the game you just closed: the place you already go to manage what you carry.
options.viewport: A category column on smoked black, Serana’s memories as a sortable item list with a details pane, and the quick toggles as a menu row.
options.risk: The most familiar direction for this audience, and the one most runs here would ship: it can read as a SkyUI clone rather than its own tool.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Everything is a numbered catalog entry on matte black.
options.viewport: A numbered index of memories with coded colour strips.
options.case: Fuses poorly: coded labels hide the words a fixer needs, and modders don’t see their game in it.
options.kept: Every record carries its catalog number.
options.risk: Codes instead of words fail a working screen.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.thesis: State drawn as hatch density over a zone ramp.
options.viewport: Overlapping sheets for each character, hatched by load.
options.case: Fuses poorly: darkroom craft is foreign to this audience, and sliding sheets hide the list.
options.kept: Tabular quantities and importance as density.
options.risk: A photographer’s costume on a game tool.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: Each change is a coupon that stamps its state.
options.viewport: A coupon book of edits, each leg torn off when saved.
options.case: Fuses poorly: travel paperwork has nothing to do with Skyrim, and coupons make editing feel bureaucratic.
options.kept: Nothing disappears; it stamps its state.
options.risk: Ephemera charm over a working list.

options.label: Guide Map
options.thesis: Each section is a swelling lobe of flat colour.
options.viewport: Sections as coloured lobes with capsule controls.
options.case: Fuses poorly: playful lobes fight dense records, and the audience has no tie to it.

options.label: Title Wall
options.thesis: Rows of tiles; the focused one grows and explains itself.
options.viewport: Characters as poster rows, one expanding on focus.
options.case: Fuses poorly: there’s no artwork to carry it, and rows hide counts and states.
options.kept: Focus lifts one item while the rest dims.
options.risk: A browsing UI for a fixing task.

options.label: Warm App
options.thesis: Soft cards, plain labels, one colour for actions.
options.viewport: One column of cards with a bottom bar.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a phone-first consumer feel for a desktop power tool, with nothing of Skyrim in it.
options.kept: The action colour appears only where something can be done.
options.risk: Generic and too loose for dense records.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A neutral dark tool UI, like the best developer tools, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Left navigation, a list pane and a detail pane, quick toggles in a top bar.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any other tool by design.
